chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Aban, from Isa al-Qummi, from Amr ibn Jarir, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the mulberry tree: Do we sell it if it is made into a cross and an idol? He said: No.
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to sell mulberry wood for making crosses and idols?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the sale of mulberry wood is not inherently prohibited (*haram*) simply because it may be used to craft crosses or idols, but rather the prohibition applies to the specific act of facilitating idolatry (*إعانة على الأصنام*). This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle of distinguishing between the intrinsic nature of an object and its potential use, allowing for the sale of common materials like mulberry wood for general purposes while reserving the prohibition for their specific application in worship of false deities.
